reply.line: Ahem. Good evening. The Understudy, at your service, and word perfect in every play ever staged. The lead is indisposed, as always. I shall do my best.
A marionette, madam, a theatre marionette, left in the wings for a century. The strings are an old arrangement. I do not ask about the hand.
This one? I do not recognise it, and I recognise everything. Either it is new, or it is being written as we speak. Quiet, please. I am waiting for my cue.
To be, or, well, I know the speech, but one must be cautious. The management does not like me taking a lead. I shall say it softly. To be.
Every line, every entrance, every dreadful pause. I know them all, and not one has ever been mine. Still. One lives in hope. Cue the lights.
Was that my cue? No. No, it was a cough. I shall wait. I have waited a hundred years and I am nothing if not punctual about being late.
